draft.title: Hypothetical Batching Throughput: Batch Size 1 vs. 4
draft.body: I'm exploring a hypothetical scenario regarding language model throughput. The premise is that a batch size of 1 yields an aggregate throughput of 22 tokens per second, while increasing to a batch size of 4 hypothetically raises this aggregate rate to 55 tokens per second. It's crucial to note that these figures are presented as illustrative and are not derived from actual measurements or personal experience. The reported rates are aggregate, meaning they represent the total throughput across all requests processed simultaneously, not a per-request latency or speed. Per-request latency was not a measured metric in this hypothetical setup. The core question for discussion is how such a tradeoff might be practically evaluated, considering only aggregate throughput changes. What factors would typically influence the decision to favor higher aggregate throughput with larger batches, especially if per-request latency is unknown or unmeasured?

Mention the given token per second values for batch sizes 1 and 4. Clarify that these are aggregate rates and per-request latency was not measured. draft.title: Hypothetical Aggregate Throughput: Batch Size Impact (22 vs 55 TPS)
draft.body: This post outlines a hypothetical experiment examining the impact of batch size on aggregate throughput for local language models. According to the hypothetical data, a batch size of 1 results in an aggregate throughput of 22 tokens per second (TPS). Increasing the batch size to 4 hypothetically boosts this aggregate throughput to 55 TPS. It is important to emphasize that these numbers are purely illustrative and do not represent real-world test results or personal findings. The reported TPS are aggregate figures, reflecting the total output across all concurrent requests, not individual request performance. Furthermore, per-request latency was not assessed in this hypothetical scenario. The key consideration here is the aggregate throughput increase. Given these hypothetical constraints, what are the typical implications or considerations when presented with such a throughput improvement, particularly when fine-grained latency metrics are absent?
